title: How Many Times Can You Retake the Florida Real Estate Exam?
metaDesc: There's no official limit on retakes, but your 2-year DBPR application window, a 24-hour wait between attempts, and the exam fee each time all matter.
h1: How Many Times Can You Retake the Florida Real Estate Exam?
about: How many times you can retake the Florida real estate sales associate exam, and what actually limits you

hub.name: Become a Real Estate Agent in Florida

answer: There's no official limit on how many times you can retake Florida's real estate sales associate exam. What actually constrains you is your DBPR application, which stays valid for two years from approval, and you have to pass within that window. You can reschedule as soon as 24 hours after a failed attempt, subject to seat availability, and each attempt requires a new exam fee.
takeaways: Florida sets no cap on the number of exam attempts. You can retake it as many times as needed.
The real limit is your DBPR application window: two years from approval to pass the exam, or you'd need to reapply.
You can reschedule as soon as 24 hours after a failed attempt, depending on seat availability at your test center.
Each retake requires paying the exam fee again. It isn't included after the first attempt.
Failing isn't unusual and doesn't affect your ability to apply again within your window. It's a graded exam, not a background check.
tldr: Florida doesn't cap how many times you can retake the real estate sales associate exam. The real constraint is time: your DBPR application is valid for two years from approval, and you need to pass within that window. You can reschedule 24 hours after a failed attempt and pay the exam fee again each time.
body:
Is there an official limit on exam retakes in Florida?

No. The Florida Department of Business and Professional Regulation doesn't set a maximum number of attempts for the real estate sales associate exam. If you fail, you can schedule another attempt. This surprises some candidates who assume a licensing exam works like a driving test with a hard cap.

So what actually limits how many times you can retake it?

Your DBPR application itself has a shelf life: it's valid for two years from the date it's approved. You need to pass the state exam within that two-year window, or your application expires and you'd need to start the application process over, including the associated fee. That's the real constraint, not a rule about attempt count.

How soon can you retake it after failing?

You can reschedule as early as 24 hours after a failed attempt, though your actual test date depends on seat availability at your chosen test center. Popular locations and times can book out, so if you fail, checking availability right away rather than waiting is worth doing.

Does it cost money every time you retake it?

Yes. The exam fee applies to each attempt, not just the first. Budget for the possibility of more than one sitting rather than assuming a single fee covers you until you pass.

Does failing the exam affect your license once you do pass?

No. Once you pass and complete licensing, your record doesn't carry a note about how many attempts it took. Plenty of licensed, successful agents didn't pass on their first try. What matters afterward is the license itself, not the path to it.

What to do differently if you've failed more than once

If you've failed multiple times, it's worth honestly assessing whether the gap is content knowledge, test-taking nerves, or timing, since the fix is different for each. Some candidates benefit from a focused review course or practice exams rather than simply rescheduling and hoping for a different result.

Once you pass: what's next

Passing the exam is a milestone, not the finish line. You'll still need to activate your license under a sponsoring broker before you can legally practice. faq.q: Is there a maximum number of times you can take the Florida real estate exam?
faq.a: No official maximum. You can retake it as many times as needed, as long as you stay within your DBPR application's two-year approval window.

faq.q: How long is your Florida real estate application valid for retaking the exam?
faq.a: Two years from the date your DBPR application is approved. You need to pass the exam within that window or your application expires.

faq.q: How soon can I retake the exam after failing?
faq.a: As soon as 24 hours after a failed attempt, subject to seat availability at your test center.

faq.q: Do you pay the exam fee every time you retake it?
faq.a: Yes. The exam fee applies to each attempt, not just your first sitting.

faq.q: Does failing the exam show up on your license record once you pass?
faq.a: No. Once licensed, your record doesn't note how many attempts it took to pass.
